strings.name: Brian Cornell
strings.role: Executive Chair and former CEO of Target
strings.summary: Brian Cornell is an American retail executive who served as Target's chair and CEO from 2014 to early 2026 before becoming executive chair. He previously led Sam's Club and PepsiCo Americas Foods and also serves on the boards of Yum! Brands and Circana.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026, with the October 16 Business Council announcement as recent evidence. Executive chair and CEO roles, divisional and group responsibilities, announcement and effective dates, and future arrangements are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads Target's retail business, advancing its brand, store experience and integration of online and offline operations.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: He earned a BA from UCLA in 1981. The university also lists a 1991 certificate, which is not presented as an MBA degree.
strings.facts.f2.label: Board responsibilities
strings.facts.f2.value: He is executive chair of Target, non-executive chair of Yum! Brands and a Circana director. These responsibilities differ from those of a CEO.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Retail and consumer-goods management
strings.highlights.h1.text: His career spans retailers and consumer-goods suppliers, providing experience in store operations, brands and supply-chain management.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Leadership transition and board service
strings.highlights.h2.text: After ending his tenure as Target CEO, he continues board work and transition support while holding governance roles at other companies.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Comments on Business Council succession
strings.timeline.t1.text: The Council announces that David Solomon will succeed him as chair and quotes his support for his successor. The announcement does not specify an exact effective date.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Appointment to Circana board announced
strings.timeline.t2.text: He is announced alongside two other new directors to help govern the consumer and market research company, rather than become its CEO.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becomes Target executive chair
strings.timeline.t3.text: Michael Fiddelke succeeds him as CEO. A subsequent agreement anticipates service as executive chair or special adviser until March 2027, without guaranteeing his chairmanship for that period.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Receives the 2022 Wooden leadership award
strings.timeline.t4.text: UCLA Anderson holds the award dinner in Los Angeles. The award is for 2022, while the presentation takes place in 2023.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becomes non-executive chair of Yum!
strings.timeline.t5.text: He succeeds Robert D. Walter. The non-executive chair's board duties are distinct from the CEO's day-to-day management.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes Target chair and CEO
strings.timeline.t6.text: He also joins the board. The appointment is announced on July 31 and becomes effective on August 12.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Leads PepsiCo Americas Foods
strings.timeline.t7.text: He serves as CEO of PepsiCo Americas Foods until July 2014. This is a divisional role.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Becomes Sam's Club CEO
strings.timeline.t8.text: He serves as president and CEO of Sam's Club and executive vice president of Walmart until January 2012.
